gloss: to feel refreshed; to feel better; to cheer up

definitions.gloss: to feel refreshed; to feel better; to cheer up; to have one's spirits lift
definitions.explanation: A feeling of emotional relief or brightening, as if clouds have cleared from one's mind. Used when worries or gloom dissipate and one feels lighter.

examples.japanese: {散歩|さんぽ}して{気|き}が{晴|は}れた。
examples.english: I took a walk and felt refreshed.

examples.japanese: {友達|ともだち}と{話|はな}したら、{少|すこ}し{気|き}が{晴|は}れた。
examples.english: After talking with my friend, I felt a bit better.

examples.japanese: ずっと{悩|なや}んでいたが、{思|おも}い{切|き}って{相談|そうだん}したら{気|き}が{晴|は}れた。
examples.english: I had been worrying for a long time, but when I took the plunge and talked to someone about it, I felt much better.

notes:
A {気|き} idiom. {晴|は}れる literally means 'to clear up' (as in weather), so the image is of clouds lifting from one's mind. Implies that the person was in a gloomy or burdened state beforehand.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {気|き}が{晴|は}れない — to not be able to cheer up
- {気|き}が{晴|は}れる{思|おも}い — a refreshing feeling
- やっと{気|き}が{晴|は}れた — I finally feel better

USAGE:
The negative form {気|き}が{晴|は}れない (can't cheer up, can't shake the feeling) is equally common and describes lingering unease or dissatisfaction.

RELATED {気|き} EXPRESSIONS:
- {気|き}が{重|おも}い — to feel heavy-hearted
- {気|き}が{楽|らく}になる — to feel at ease
- {気分|きぶん}{転換|てんかん} — a change of pace (noun)
